title: Tangshan earthquake
summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Tangshan, an industrial and coal-mining city in Hebei, at 3:42 a.m. on 28 July 1976. Official counts give about 240,000 to 242,000 dead, while estimates in the first two years ranged from 650,000 to 800,000; USGS says the exact number will almost certainly never be known.

uncertainty.note: USGS gives 3:42 a.m. on July 28, 1976, without a time zone; EBSCO gives the date and a magnitude range of 7.5 to 8.2 across the main shock and aftershocks.

where.modern_name: Tangshan, Hebei, China (city point; epicentre not stated on the opened pages)
where.historical_name: Tangshan, Hebei Province, People's Republic of China

importance.justification: One of the deadliest earthquakes of the twentieth century, destroying an industrial city.

audience_note: Describes a disaster with very large loss of life. Death tolls are given as attributed, disputed figures.

beats.caption: At 3:42 a.m. a magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes Tangshan, a city of about one million on a fault line.
Official counts are 240,000 to 242,000 dead; estimates in the first two years ranged from 650,000 to 800,000.
The government issued its official toll of 242,000 only in 1979, three years later, and critics cite far higher figures.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the pin is the city point, not the epicentre (no opened page gives epicentre coordinates). Death toll ranges: USGS official 240,000 and 650,000-800,000 estimates; EBSCO official 242,000 (issued 1979) and 655,000 attributed to the Hebei Revolutionary Committee as cited by critics. Magnitude 7.8 is USGS; EBSCO gives 7.5-8.2.
